To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
glucose transporters 3 and 1 are expressed sequentially in different layers of the placental membranes of the ruminant.
Glucose transporters are localised to different membranes of the synepitheilochorial placenta of ruminants.
glucose transporters are localised in different membrane layers of ruminant placentae.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the localisation of glucose transport across the ruminant placentome.
the localisation of glucose transporters in the ruminants and the implications for sequential use by the transporter isoforms.
the localisation of the facilitative glucose transporter proteins (GLUTs) in the ruminants, and the functional implications of this localisation for glucose transport across the ruminant placentas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the placenta of ruminants is characterised by the expression of both GT1 and GT 3 in a sequential manner to allow glucose transfer from the maternal to the fetal circulation.

GT1 and GT1 are localised on the microvillar and basolateral membranes of the syncytial and trophoblastic cells respectively, and that glucose must pass sequentially from maternal to fetal circulation via both isoforms.
GT1 and GT2 are the major routes of glucose transport across ruminant placental membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the placenta of all ruminant species examined has a similar pattern of localisation for GT1 and GT 3 and that glucose utilisation is sequential and involves the use of both isoforms.
GT1 is localised on microvilli of the trophoblast, GT3 is localised on syncytiotrophoblast, and both are localised on the endothelium and the basal plasma membranes of the trophoectoderm.
glucose transport in the placenta is localised to the apical membranes of the trophoblast and endothelial cells and the basolateral membranes of the endothelial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GT1 and GT 3 are both present on the placental barrier and are expressed in a complementary manner.
the expression patterns of GT1 and GT2 in the ruminants are very similar to those in humans, and that the placenta is an important site for GT expression in ruminants, as it is in humans.
the placenta has to be considered as a barrier that can be traversed sequentially by glucose.
